# Baton — Engineering Handovers with Evidence

> Baton is engineering handover software that keeps decision records, open work, ownership, and unresolved risks together in one reviewable handover, with source evidence attached to every claim — so the next owner can review the handover with confidence instead of archaeology. Built for engineering teams, tech leads, SREs, and platform teams navigating ownership changes.

Key concepts:

- **Decision records**: every decision captures the choice, the rationale, and the next action, linked to the pull request, incident, ticket, or runbook it came from.
- **Open work**: unfinished items carry an owner and the next step, so nothing is silently dropped during an ownership transfer.
- **Ownership transfer**: leaver, lead, and successor each attest their part; the handover closes with an accepted sign-off.
- **Unresolved risks**: contradictions between sources enter a human review queue and stay visible until a lead settles them with a recorded rationale.
- **Source evidence**: claims in the ledger are pinned to verbatim excerpts from their source systems — never paraphrased away.

Trying Baton:

- [Sign in](https://www.gitlostbaton.xyz/signin): GitHub sign-in for live repository imports, plus pre-configured review seats (successor, lead, leaver) that need no setup.
- [How it works](https://www.gitlostbaton.xyz/#how-it-works): the capture → review → handover workflow on the landing page.
- [Core capabilities](https://www.gitlostbaton.xyz/#capabilities): decision logs, risk registers, ownership sign-offs, and audit trails.
- [FAQ](https://www.gitlostbaton.xyz/#faq): what a Baton handover is, how claims are verified, and how privacy works.

Project:

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/26f2000861-AV/baton): source code, README, and documentation.
- [Issue tracker](https://github.com/26f2000861-AV/baton/issues): report problems or ask questions.

Notes:

- The public walkthrough uses a synthetic sample case; no live source systems are connected in the demonstration environment.
- Workspace data is reader-scoped and private per seat.
